title: First playing with a Black musician, with Louis Prima in 1937
summary: He never played with a Black musician in New Orleans; the first time was with Prima's band in California in 1937.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Never. Never did sit in with a colored musician. Oddly enough, when I first, when I went to California with Louis Prima in 1937, we had a piano player, I don't remember his name, but he was a great piano, relief piano player. And we'd get on the stand to play while he was, and Louis would say, keep on playing. He said, you and Louis, because Frank Venera wasn't the greatest pianist in the world for jazz. And Louis would let him play with us and get the band on and say, believe me, that was the first colored fellow that I ever played with, and I felt like a, like a woman losing her virginity, playing with a colored man for the first time. Believe me, you didn't, you didn't do those things in New Orleans. Do you remember anything like that?
Well, I can remember that, sure, up into the 60s or so, not a problem with anybody who tried to do that. Well, the funniest thing
